spark_open.description: The creature is shown in right lateral profile standing on a small patch of ground, facing to the right. It is a stout, quadrupedal, amphibian-like animal with a broad flattened head, a thick elongated trunk, four short muscular limbs, and a long laterally compressed tail that extends off the left edge of the image and bears a continuous low dorsal fin-fold along its upper edge. The skin is wrinkled and granular, mottled gray-brown dorsally fading to pale cream on the belly and flanks where it forms prominent transverse annular ridges. Behind the head are six feathery external gill stalks with dense pinkish-red filaments, three visible on each side. On the dorsal mid-back, on the shoulder region, and on the hip/thigh region there are three discrete patches of overlapping large brown keratinous scales. The overall impression is of a single composite animal combining amphibian body form with armored scale patches.

meta_spark.description: A large stout salamander-like creature shown in right-facing side view with a thick elongated body, four short muscular legs, and a long tapering tail. Its skin is smooth but deeply wrinkled and ribbed along the flanks, gray-brown above fading to pale cream below. The head is broad and flat with a rounded snout, large round dark eyes, a thin smiling mouth slit, and tiny nostrils at the tip. Behind the head are six long tapered external gill stalks, three per side, bearing dense pink feathery filaments. Along the back and sides are three distinct patches of overlapping rounded brown plate-like scales. The tail extends to the left with a low dark fin-like ridge along its upper edge.
